task_title: Airport Operations, Light Signals and Runway Safety
objective: By the end of this lesson you can fly a non-towered arrival and departure the way the rules and AC 90-66C describe, taxi at a towered airport using clearances, signs, markings and light signals correctly, and spot the moments when a runway incursion is most likely.
why: Runway incursions are mostly pilot deviations, and general aviation pilots cause most of those. Several taxi rules changed after many pilots trained, such as the explicit clearance now needed for every runway crossing. Airport markings and operations, 91.125 and 91.126 are all on the AC 61-98E flight review checklist.

prereading.what: Light gun signals, the Class G and Class E airport rules, and the Class D radio, approach and clearance rules. Short, and every word counts.
prereading.label: 14 CFR 91.125 to 91.129

prereading.what: The current FAA guide to non-towered airport flying: pattern flow, radio calls, entries, departures and straight-ins.
prereading.label: AC 90-66C 8 to 11.10

prereading.what: CTAF, self-announce calls and when to make them (TBL 4-1-1).
prereading.label: AIM 4-1-9

prereading.what: Light signals, tower and ground frequencies, taxi clearances, readbacks and exiting the runway.
prereading.label: AIM 4-3-13 to 4-3-21

prereading.what: Holding position markings and the airport signs that go with them.
prereading.label: AIM 2-3-5 to 2-3-10

prereading.what: Single-pilot taxi procedures to avoid causing a runway incursion: planning, briefing, readbacks and lights.
prereading.label: AC 91-73B 7

prereading.what: Runway incursion definition, categories, causes and the six steps the FAA recommends.
prereading.label: AC 61-98E 2-6 to 2-11

warmup: Think first: Ground tells you "Runway 27, taxi via Alpha." Alpha crosses Runway 31 on the way. Twenty years ago, many pilots would have taxied across 31 without another word. Can you today? And at a non-towered field, who decides when it is safe to cross that same hold line?

key_terms.def: The frequency for airport advisory calls at an airport without an operating tower. It may be a UNICOM, MULTICOM, FSS or tower frequency.
Broadcasting your call sign, position, altitude and intentions on the CTAF so other pilots know where you are.
The frequency to self-announce on at an airport with no tower, FSS or UNICOM.
The direction of turns in the pattern. 91.126(b) regulates it (left unless marked right). The FAA does not regulate how you enter.
Runways, taxiways and other areas used for taxiing, takeoff and landing, not counting loading ramps and parking areas. At a towered airport you need approval to enter it.
Four yellow lines across the taxiway, two solid and two dashed. The solid lines are on the side where you must stop.
White letters outlined in black on a red background. It marks a runway entrance, a critical area, or an area you may not enter.
Yellow dashes on both sides of the taxiway centerline for up to 150 ft before a runway holding position marking. It means get ready to stop.
A place on the movement area with a history of potential risk of collision or runway incursion, where pilots need extra care.
Any occurrence at an aerodrome where an aircraft, vehicle or person is wrongly present on the protected area of a surface used for landing and takeoff.
An instruction to taxi onto the runway and hold in position. It is not a takeoff clearance.
Automatic red in-pavement lights that show a runway is unsafe to enter, cross or take off on. They never give you a clearance.

chunks.title: Non-towered airports: what the rules require

body.p: At an airport in Class G with no operating control tower, each airplane approaching to land must make all turns to the left. The only exception is when the airport shows approved light signals or visual markings for right turns [[60:451|14 CFR 91.126(b)]]. 91.127 applies the same rule at airports in Class E [[60:452|14 CFR 91.127(a)]], and 91.129 adds both sections for Class D [[60:452|14 CFR 91.129(a)]].

callout.text: The FAA regulates traffic pattern flow, not pattern entry. Pilots arriving are expected to watch the traffic already there and conform to the pattern in use [[17:4|AC 90-66C 8.2.1]]. An aircraft in the traffic pattern counts as approaching to land, so it must use the published turn direction [[17:4|AC 90-66C 8.2.1.1]].

body.p: An aircraft outside the pattern, such as one crossing midfield above pattern altitude to enter, is not bound by 91.126(b). When a towered airport's tower is closed, the 91.126 flow rules still apply in Class E, D or C airspace [[17:4|AC 90-66C 8.2.1.1 Note]].

bullets: On sectional and terminal charts, RP followed by runway numbers marks the runways with right traffic [[2:16|Chart Users' Guide p 16]]. If no RP is shown, assume a left pattern [[17:4|AC 90-66C 8.2.1.1 Note]].
*RP means special conditions exist: read the Chart Supplement [[33:240|AIM 4-3-3d]].
Right patterns are not charted at airports with full-time towers [[33:240|AIM 4-3-3d]].
On the ground, a segmented circle may hold traffic pattern indicators. They show the turn direction when it differs from the normal left pattern [[33:244|AIM 4-3-4b5]].

callout.text: Mentally enlarge the traffic pattern indicator for the runway you will use. The base and final legs then become obvious [[33:244|AIM 4-3-4c]]. The small end of a tetrahedron points the direction of landing; do not use it to judge the wind [[33:244|AIM 4-3-4b3]].
FSS airport advisories are available only in Alaska [[33:206|AIM 4-1-9a2]]. Elsewhere, you self-announce or talk to a UNICOM [[33:206|AIM 4-1-9a2]].

check.q: Pittsfield's chart block says "RP 26, 32." You will land on Runway 32. Which way do you turn in the pattern?
check.a: To the right. RP lists the runways that use a right pattern [[2:16|Chart Users' Guide p 16]], and right turns are required where the airport marks them [[60:451|14 CFR 91.126(b)]].

head: Situation
What AC 90-66C, the AIM and the AFH recommend
rows: Pattern altitude

Propeller airplanes 1,000 ft above the airport unless a different altitude is published [[17:23|AC 90-66C A-5]]. Large and turbine airplanes not less than 1,500 ft AGL or 500 ft above the pattern altitude [[33:239|AIM 4-3-3a]]
Arriving from the downwind side
At pattern altitude, level, on a 45 degree angle to downwind abeam the runway midpoint [[17:15|AC 90-66C 11.3]]
Arriving from the upwind side (preferred)

Cross midfield at least 500 ft above pattern altitude, normally 1,500 ft AGL, or 2,000 ft AGL if large or turbine aircraft use the airport. About 2 miles clear, descend to pattern altitude and turn back to the 45 entry [[24:168|AFH 8-4]] [[17:23|AC 90-66C A-5]]
Arriving from the upwind side (alternate)
Midfield crosswind entry at pattern altitude, then turn downwind. Not when the pattern is busy [[24:168|AFH 8-4]] [[17:19|AC 90-66C A-1]]
Straight-in
Discouraged. If you fly one, self-announce 8 to about 10 miles out and coordinate. You get no priority, and 91.113(g) still applies [[17:8|AC 90-66C 9.11.1]]
Downwind to base
Hold pattern altitude until at least abeam the approach end; start base about 45 degrees from the approach end [[17:15|AC 90-66C 11.4]]
Takeoff or go-around
Straight ahead until past the departure end [[17:15|AC 90-66C 11.6]]. Staying in the pattern: turn crosswind past the departure end and within 300 ft of pattern altitude [[17:15|AC 90-66C 11.7]]
Leaving the pattern
Straight out, or a 45 degree turn in the pattern direction, past the departure end after reaching pattern altitude [[17:15|AC 90-66C 11.8]]

callout.text: Do not descend into the pattern. A descending aircraft can come down on top of one already there, so all similar aircraft should be at the same pattern altitude [[17:19|AC 90-66C A-1]] [[17:15|AC 90-66C 11.3]].

91.113(g): the aircraft at the lower altitude has the right-of-way when two are approaching to land, but it may not use that to cut in front of one on final or to overtake it [[60:448|14 CFR 91.113(g)]].

body.p: Use the runway most nearly aligned into the wind. If you need a secondary runway, stay out of the flow to the main one [[17:15|AC 90-66C 11.5]]. If other traffic is in the pattern, use the same runway they are using [[17:8|AC 90-66C 9.11]].

check.q: Staying in the pattern after a touch-and-go, when may you turn crosswind?
check.a: After you are past the departure end of the runway and within 300 ft of pattern altitude [[17:15|AC 90-66C 11.7]].

body.p: The CTAF may be a UNICOM, MULTICOM, FSS or tower frequency; it is listed in the Chart Supplement and on approach charts [[33:206|AIM 4-1-9b1]] [[33:207|AIM 4-1-9b3]]. If an airport has no tower, FSS or UNICOM, self-announce on MULTICOM 122.9 [[33:209|AIM 4-1-9g3]]. If a tower is closed or part-time and no FSS is open, self-announce on the CTAF [[33:209|AIM 4-1-9g2]].

head: When
What to do
rows: Departing
Call before taxiing and before taxiing onto the runway [[33:207|AIM TBL 4-1-1]]. Monitor from engine start, during taxi, and until 10 miles out [[33:207|AIM 4-1-9c1]]
Arriving
Call 10 miles out, then entering downwind, base and final, and when leaving the runway [[33:207|AIM TBL 4-1-1]]. Monitor from 10 miles to landing [[33:207|AIM 4-1-9c1]]
Overflying or practicing at pattern altitudes
Monitor and talk on the CTAF while within 10 miles [[33:207|AIM 4-1-9c2]]

bullets: Say the airport name at the start and end of each call, and use the runway number, not "active runway" [[33:209|AIM 4-1-9g8]].
Use the airport's published name, not the town's [[17:12|AC 90-66C 10.1]].
Include your aircraft type. Do not replace the call sign with paint colors [[17:7|AC 90-66C 9.8.1]].
"Traffic in the area, please advise" is not a recognized phrase; do not use it [[33:209|AIM 4-1-9g1]].
Do not broadcast your own landing sequence ("number 3"). Sequencing is ATC's job at towered airports [[17:13|AC 90-66C 10.1 Note]].
Avoid the words "to" and "for"; they can be mistaken for runway numbers or altitudes [[17:13|AC 90-66C 10.3]].

body.p: Example, built on the AIM format (application): "Pittsfield traffic, Skyhawk one two three four X, entering right downwind runway two six, full stop, Pittsfield" [[33:209|AIM 4-1-9g8]].

callout.text: Radio calls are not the whole picture. No-radio aircraft may be in the pattern, so keep looking [[17:10|AC 90-66C 9.12.2]]. A UNICOM operator does not have to answer you, and there is no standard for what it says [[17:5|AC 90-66C 9.3]].

Pilot-controlled lighting: key the mike 7 times within 5 seconds for full intensity, then 5 or 3 times to lower it. The lights stay on 15 minutes from the last activation [[33:132|AIM 2-1-8b-c]]. The frequency is in the Chart Supplement, not on the sectional [[33:132|AIM 2-1-8d]].

check.q: The part-time tower closed an hour ago and there is no FSS. What frequency do you use, and when should you first call?
check.a: Self-announce on the published CTAF [[33:209|AIM 4-1-9g2]], starting when you are about 10 miles from the airport [[17:7|AC 90-66C 9.8]].

chunks.title: Towered airports: radio contact and clearances

callout.text: To, from, through or on any airport with an operating control tower, in Class G or Class E, you must keep two-way radio contact with the tower. Establish it before 4 NM from the airport, up to and including 2,500 ft AGL [[60:452|14 CFR 91.126(d)]] [[60:452|14 CFR 91.127(c)]]. In Class D, establish two-way radio contact before entering, and keep it while inside [[60:453|14 CFR 91.129(c)(1)]].

At any airport with an operating control tower, you may not operate on a runway or taxiway, take off, or land without an appropriate ATC clearance [[60:454|14 CFR 91.129(i)]]. You also need approval before moving onto the movement area [[33:260|AIM 4-3-18a]].

bullets: Make the first call about 15 miles out [[33:237|AIM 4-3-2a]].
Unless the tower says otherwise, airplanes circle the airport to the left [[60:454|14 CFR 91.129(f)(1)]], and a landing clearance is always required [[33:237|AIM 4-3-2b]].
Some towered airports have no Class D because they lack weather reporting. You still talk to the tower [[33:237|AIM 4-3-2a]].
Departing: call ground or clearance delivery before starting the engine, stay on ground through taxi and run-up, then switch to tower when ready [[33:257|AIM 4-3-14a]].
After landing, stay on tower until the controller tells you to switch to ground [[33:258|AIM 4-3-14c]].
Planning a low approach inside a Class B, C or D surface area? Ask the tower for approval before you start the final approach [[33:256|AIM 4-3-12b]].
In Class D, airplanes landing on a runway with a visual approach slope indicator stay at or above the glide path until lower is needed to land safely [[60:453|14 CFR 91.129(e)(3)]].

callout.text: Do not assume the tower's radar means full radar service or constant monitoring [[33:239|AIM 4-3-2e]]. A suggested heading from the tower is advice, and seeing and avoiding traffic is still yours [[33:239|AIM 4-3-2d3]].

body.p: The final decision rests with you. If you cannot safely comply with an instruction, say "unable" [[1:367|PHAK 14-33]].

check.q: A towered airport sits in Class E with no Class D. Where must you be in two-way radio contact with the tower?
check.a: Before 4 NM from the airport, up to and including 2,500 ft AGL, and while operating to, from, through or on the airport [[60:452|14 CFR 91.127(c)]].

chunks.title: Taxi instructions, hold short and runway crossings

body.p: Call ground with who you are, where you are on the airport, what you want and what you know (the ATIS code) [[7:8|AC 91-73B 7f(2)]]. The AIM adds the type of operation (VFR or IFR) and your first intended landing point [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18d1]].

callout.text: Changed: since June 30, 2010, ATC must give explicit instructions to cross or hold short of each runway, whether active, inactive or closed [[1:368|PHAK 14-34]]. You need a clearance before crossing any runway [[33:260|AIM 4-3-18a5]]. A runway assignment does not let you enter or cross that departure runway at any point [[33:260|AIM 4-3-18a6]], and ground's taxi clearance to parking does not let you enter or cross any runway [[33:264|AIM 4-3-21c Note 2]].

head: Who
Says
Why
rows: You
"Riverton ground, Skyhawk one two three four X, at the FBO, VFR to the south, with information Bravo."
Who, where, what you want, what you know (application of [[7:8|AC 91-73B 7f(2)]])
Ground
"Skyhawk three four X, Runway two seven, taxi via Alpha, hold short of Runway three one."
Runway first, then route, then hold short [[33:260|AIM 4-3-18a6]]
You
"Skyhawk three four X, Runway two seven via Alpha, hold short Runway three one."
Read back runway, route and hold short [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18a9]]
Ground (later)
"Skyhawk three four X, cross Runway three one."
Each crossing gets its own clearance [[1:368|PHAK 14-34]]

bullets: Always read back the runway assignment, any clearance to enter a specific runway, and any instruction to hold short of a runway or line up and wait [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18a9]]. ATC must get a readback of every runway hold short instruction [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18b1 Note]].
Use your full call sign and the runway number in these readbacks, not "Roger" or "Wilco" [[7:8|AC 91-73B 7f(4)]].
"Hold short" means no part of the airplane past the runway holding position marking [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5a1]].
Line up and wait is not a takeoff clearance [[1:368|PHAK 14-34]]. If no word comes within 90 seconds, call ATC [[1:369|PHAK 14-35]] [[7:6|AC 91-73B 7d(9)]].

body.p: After landing, exit without delay at the first available taxiway or where ATC tells you. Do not exit onto another runway without ATC authorization, and do not stop or reverse on the runway without approval [[33:264|AIM 4-3-21a]]. You are not clear of the runway until all parts of the airplane have crossed the holding position marking [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5a1]]; then hold unless ATC has given further instructions [[33:264|AIM 4-3-21b]]. No clearance is needed to cross that marking as you exit [[1:342|PHAK 14-8]].

callout.text: Unsure of the route? Ask for progressive taxi, which gives step-by-step directions [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18b3]]. Write complex instructions down [[7:7|AC 91-73B 7e]].

check.q: Ground says "Runway 27, taxi via Alpha." Alpha crosses Runway 31 and ends at Runway 27. How far may you go?
check.a: Only to the Runway 31 holding position marking. Every runway crossing needs an explicit clearance [[33:260|AIM 4-3-18a5]], and the runway assignment does not let you enter Runway 27 either [[33:260|AIM 4-3-18a6]].

body.p: These meanings are regulation, in 91.125 [[60:451|14 CFR 91.125]]. Towers use light signals for aircraft and vehicles without a radio, and for radio-equipped ones when contact cannot be made [[33:256|AIM 4-3-13a]] [[33:257|AIM 4-3-13a]].

callout.text: Memory aid (not FAA wording): steady green is the big "go" (takeoff or land). Flashing green is the small go (taxi, or come around). Steady red is "stop" (or give way and keep circling). Flashing red is "get away" (clear the runway, or do not land). Flashing white sends you home to your starting point. Red and green together means extreme caution [[60:451|14 CFR 91.125]].

bullets: Limits: you may not be looking at the tower, and lights can only approve or disapprove what you seem to be doing. Only the general warning signal adds anything [[33:257|AIM 4-3-13b]].
Acknowledge by day by moving the ailerons or rudder, and at night by blinking the landing or navigation lights [[33:257|AIM 4-3-13e]].
At night on the ground, to get the tower's attention, turn on the landing light and taxi clear of the active runway to where the tower can see it [[33:257|AIM 4-3-13c]].
If the radio fails after you leave parking, watch the tower for light signals or monitor tower frequency [[33:257|AIM 4-3-13e]].

callout.text: VFR radio failure in Class D: you may land if the weather is at or above basic VFR minimums, you keep visual contact with the tower, and you receive a clearance to land [[60:453|14 CFR 91.129(d)(2)]]. The same applies at towered airports in Class G and E [[60:452|14 CFR 91.126(d)]]. Where ATC has approved operating without two-way radio, or radio contact cannot be made with a tower not run by the U.S. Government, get a light signal clearance before taxiing on a runway and before takeoff and landing [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18c]].
If the frequency goes unusually quiet, suspect a radio problem or a stuck microphone: contact ATC and look for light gun signals [[7:6|AC 91-73B 7d(9) Note]].

check.q: Your radio quits while you taxi toward the runway. The tower points a flashing red light at you. What does it mean?
check.a: Taxi clear of the runway in use [[60:451|14 CFR 91.125]].

chunks.title: Signs and markings that keep you off the runway

body.p: Runway markings are white. Taxiway markings, holding position markings (even on a runway) and markings for closed or hazardous areas are yellow [[33:138|AIM 2-3-2b]].

head: Sign
How it looks
What it tells you
rows: Mandatory instruction
White letters outlined in black on red [[19:13|AC 150/5340-18H xiii]]

A runway entrance or critical area, or an area you may not enter [[33:162|AIM 2-3-8a]]. Examples: runway holding position [[33:162|AIM 2-3-8b1]], runway approach area, ILS critical area, no entry [[19:13|AC 150/5340-18H xiii]]
Location
Yellow letters and yellow border on black [[33:165|AIM 2-3-9a1]]
The taxiway or runway you are on [[33:165|AIM 2-3-9a]]
Runway boundary
Yellow, with a black drawing of the holding position marking; faces the runway [[33:166|AIM 2-3-9a3]]
A cue for when you are clear of the runway [[33:166|AIM 2-3-9a3]]
Direction
Black on yellow with arrows; normally on the left before the intersection [[33:167|AIM 2-3-10a, c]]
The taxiways leading out of the intersection, arranged clockwise from the first one on your left [[33:167|AIM 2-3-10d]]
Destination
Black on yellow, always with an arrow [[33:169|AIM 2-3-11a-b]]
The way to a place such as a runway, ramp or FBO [[33:169|AIM 2-3-11]]

body.p: On a runway holding position sign, the numbers match the thresholds: "15-33" means the Runway 15 threshold is to your left and 33 is to your right [[33:162|AIM 2-3-8b1]]. At the takeoff end, the sign may show only the takeoff runway [[33:162|AIM 2-3-8b1(a)]].

bullets: Runway holding position marking: four yellow lines, two solid and two dashed. The solid lines are always on the side where you hold [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5a]].
ILS critical area holding position: two solid lines joined by short cross lines, like a ladder. Hold there only when ATC tells you to [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5b]].
Taxiway/taxiway holding position: a single dashed line [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5c]].
Surface painted holding position sign: white on red, painted to the left of the centerline on the holding side [[33:152|AIM 2-3-5d]].
Nonmovement area boundary: one solid and one dashed yellow line; the dashed line is on the movement area side [[33:159|AIM 2-3-6c]].
Runways have white segmented centerlines; taxiways have continuous yellow ones [[7:9|AC 91-73B 7g(5)]].

body.p: The enhanced taxiway centerline adds yellow dashes on both sides of the centerline for up to 150 ft before a runway holding position marking. It warns you to prepare to stop unless ATC has cleared you onto or across the runway [[33:144|AIM 2-3-4b2]]. At Part 139 certificated airports, every taxiway that meets a runway must have one, plus a surface painted holding position sign [[20:71|AC 150/5340-1M 4-1]].

callout.text: The hold line matters at non-towered airports too. There, you must make sure of adequate separation from aircraft, vehicles and people before crossing it [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5a1]] [[19:24|AC 150/5340-18H 1-10]].

check.q: A holding position sign at your taxiway reads "9-27." Which way is the Runway 27 threshold?
check.a: To your right. The numbers are arranged to match the thresholds [[33:162|AIM 2-3-8b1]].

chunks.title: Runway safety lights and hot spots

bullets: Runway guard lights: a pair of flashing yellow lights beside the taxiway, or a row of yellow lights in the pavement, at the runway holding position [[33:133|AIM 2-1-10d]].

Stop bar: a row of red in-pavement lights across the taxiway at the holding position, used below 1,200 ft RVR. Never cross a red stop bar, even with a clearance [[33:133|AIM 2-1-10e]] [[33:134|AIM 2-1-10e]].

Runway Entrance Lights (REL): red in-pavement lights from the hold line toward the runway. Lit, they mean fast traffic on the runway or an aircraft on final within the activation area [[33:127|AIM 2-1-6b]].
Takeoff Hold Lights (THL): two rows of red lights on the runway, from 375 ft past the departure threshold for 1,500 ft. Lit, it is unsafe to take off [[33:128|AIM 2-1-6c]].
Taxiway edge lights are blue; taxiway centerline lights are green [[33:133|AIM 2-1-10a-b]].

callout.text: RWSL verifies a clearance; it never replaces one. Never cross illuminated red lights. If they conflict with your clearance, stop and tell ATC. Do not go when they turn off unless ATC has cleared you [[33:129|AIM 2-1-6d]]. At RWSL airports, keep the transponder and ADS-B on from the gate or parking area until you shut down there [[33:129|AIM 2-1-6d1]].

An airport beacon on in daylight in a Class B, C, D or E surface area often means the visibility is below 3 miles or the ceiling below 1,000 ft. No rule requires it, so don't rely on it [[33:133|AIM 2-1-9d]].

body.p: A hot spot is a place on the movement area with a history of potential risk of collision or runway incursion, where pilots need extra attention [[34:358|PCG H-3]]. Airport diagrams show it as a brown open circle or ellipse with a leader to its number, such as HS 1. The number matches a description on the hot spot page at the front of the Terminal Procedures [[2:124|Chart Users' Guide p 124]].

At Sioux Gateway, Taxiway Bravo meets two runways, 31-13 and 35-17, right where they cross each other. The PHAK calls this geometry very confusing, and it is marked as a hot spot [[1:342|PHAK 14-8]]. Find every hot spot on or near your route before you taxi [[16:9|AC 90-48E 10.1.4]] [[7:8|AC 91-73B 7g(1)]].

check.q: Tower clears you to cross Runway 9, but the red Runway Entrance Lights at your hold line are lit. What do you do?
check.a: Stay stopped at the hold line, tell ATC you are holding because of the red lights, and get the clearance confirmed [[33:127|AIM 2-1-6b4]] [[33:129|AIM 2-1-6d2-3]].

chunks.title: Risk: crossing a hold line or entering a runway without clearance

body.p: A runway incursion is any occurrence at an aerodrome involving the incorrect presence of an aircraft, vehicle or person on the protected area of a surface designated for landing and takeoff [[15:14|AC 61-98E 2.3.1]] [[7:1|AC 91-73B 1]]. The FAA sorts them into pilot deviations, operational incidents (controller errors) and vehicle or pedestrian deviations [[15:14|AC 61-98E 2.3.1]]. Category A is a near collision; Category D is an incorrect presence with no immediate safety consequences [[15:15|AC 61-98E 2.3.2]].
In fiscal year 2012, pilot deviations caused 63 percent of runway incursions, and general aviation pilots caused more than 80 percent of those deviations [[15:15|AC 61-98E 2.3.3]].

head: Main cause
What to do about it
rows: Failure to comply with ATC instructions [[15:15|AC 61-98E 2.3.4]]
Write the clearance down and read it back [[15:17|AC 61-98E 2.3.6.3.4]]. Put a reminder on a knob or the yoke when told to hold short [[7:8|AC 91-73B 7f(3)]]
Lack of airport familiarity [[15:15|AC 61-98E 2.3.4]]
Before taxi, review NOTAMs and ATIS for closures, and the airport diagram and hot spots [[7:3|AC 91-73B 7b(1)]]. Ask for progressive taxi [[15:18|AC 61-98E 2.3.6.4]]
Not following standard procedures [[15:15|AC 61-98E 2.3.4]]
Finish checklists, radios and GPS setup before moving; do heads-down tasks only when stopped [[7:6|AC 91-73B 7d Note]] [[15:17|AC 61-98E 2.3.6.3.3]]

bullets: Expectation trap: follow the clearance you actually received, not the one you expected [[7:4|AC 91-73B 7b(2) Caution]].
Similar call signs: be careful not to act on another aircraft's clearance [[7:6|AC 91-73B 7d(6)]].
Before entering or crossing any runway, be positive you are cleared, then scan the full length of the runway and the final approach. If anything is unclear, stop and ask [[7:6|AC 91-73B 7d(4)]].
Lost on the airport? Never stop on a runway. Stop, tell ATC, and ask for progressive taxi if needed [[7:9|AC 91-73B 7g(5)]].

Without a tower, nobody is watching for you. Listen on the CTAF and scan the runway and its approach and departure paths before you enter or cross; some aircraft have no radio [[7:7|AC 91-73B 7d(12)]].
Wrong runway: check that the painted runway numbers, the magnetic compass and the heading indicator all match the assigned runway [[16:10|AC 90-48E 10.4.1 Note]].

callout.text: Lights tell others what you are doing. Turn on all exterior lights when crossing a runway. When entering a runway for takeoff or line up and wait, turn on all lights except the landing lights. Turn the landing lights on when cleared for takeoff, or as you start the takeoff roll at a non-towered airport [[7:10|AC 91-73B 7h(2)]].
Familiarity is a trap too: some pilots stop reading signs at airports they know well [[15:16|AC 61-98E 2.3.6.1]].

check.q: A pilot taxis onto a runway at a towered airport without authorization. What type of incursion is it, and what were the three main pilot causes the FAA found?
check.a: A pilot deviation [[15:14|AC 61-98E 2.3.1.1]]. The causes: failure to comply with ATC instructions, lack of airport familiarity, and nonconformance with standard operating procedures [[15:15|AC 61-98E 2.3.4]].

chunks.title: Fly it: a non-towered arrival and departure, and a towered taxi

bullets: 1. Before the flight, read the Chart Supplement and NOTAMs for the pattern, CTAF, pattern altitude and runway lighting [[17:5|AC 90-66C 9.1]].
2. About 10 miles out, monitor the CTAF and self-announce position, altitude and intentions [[17:13|AC 90-66C 10.4.1]].
3. Find the runway in use from above pattern altitude, staying out of the flow, then go well clear before descending [[17:14|AC 90-66C 11.2]].
4. Enter level at pattern altitude: 45 degrees to midfield downwind, or the upwind side crossing [[17:15|AC 90-66C 11.3]] [[24:168|AFH 8-4]].
5. Call downwind, base and final, and when clear of the runway [[33:207|AIM TBL 4-1-1]].
1. Monitor the CTAF from engine start, and announce before taxiing [[33:207|AIM 4-1-9c1]] [[33:207|AIM TBL 4-1-1]].
2. Before entering the runway, make sure no one is landing toward you or on your runway, and that you will not conflict with another runway [[17:6|AC 90-66C 9.5.1]].
3. Announce the runway, your departure direction, or that you will stay in the pattern [[17:6|AC 90-66C 9.5.3]].
4. Don't sit lined up on the runway longer than you must [[7:14|AC 91-73B App 1 5]]. Back-taxiing is discouraged at non-towered airports [[17:13|AC 90-66C 10.4.2 Note]].
1. Get the ATIS, then review the diagram for hot spots and every place you must hold short [[16:9|AC 90-48E 10.3]] [[16:10|AC 90-48E 10.3.3]].
2. Call ground with your full call sign and position; write the route down and read it back [[16:10|AC 90-48E 10.3.2]].
3. Taxi heads-up, following your progress on the diagram [[7:5|AC 91-73B 7d(1)]].
4. Stop at every hold line you are not cleared past. When in doubt, stop and ask [[16:10|AC 90-48E 10.3.4]].

callout.text: The AC 61-98E flight review checklist lists airport markings, operations (91.125 and 91.126) and traffic patterns [[15:41|AC 61-98E E-2]]. A flight to a towered airport with a flight instructor is a good way to regain proficiency [[15:16|AC 61-98E 2.3.6.1]].

check.q: On a non-towered departure, what two things should you check before you taxi onto the runway?
check.a: That no aircraft is landing toward you or on your runway, and that you will not cause a conflict with another runway [[17:6|AC 90-66C 9.5.1]]. Then announce your runway and departure direction [[17:6|AC 90-66C 9.5.3]].

bullets: Treating a runway assignment as permission to cross runways on the way. Fix: hold short of every runway until you hear "cross" [[33:260|AIM 4-3-18a5]].
Answering a hold short with "Roger." Fix: read back call sign, runway and hold short [[7:8|AC 91-73B 7f(4)]].
Stopping with the tail still over the hold line after landing. Fix: roll until every part of the airplane is past it [[33:264|AIM 4-3-21b]].
Descending into the pattern or crossing midfield at pattern altitude when it is busy. Fix: enter level at pattern altitude; use the 45 [[17:15|AC 90-66C 11.3]] [[24:168|AFH 8-4]].
"Any traffic please advise" and "active runway." Fix: give your own position and the runway number [[33:209|AIM 4-1-9g]].
Trusting the radio alone at a non-towered field. Fix: look for no-radio traffic, and scan final both ways before taking the runway [[17:10|AC 90-66C 9.12.2]] [[17:6|AC 90-66C 9.5.1]].
Rolling once red RWSL lights go out. Fix: lights confirm clearances; they never give one [[33:129|AIM 2-1-6d4]].
Doing checklists or GPS entries while taxiing. Fix: do them stopped [[7:9|AC 91-73B 7g(2)]].

check.q: Why is "wilco" a poor reply to "hold short of Runway 31"?
check.a: Because ATC must get a readback of every runway hold short instruction [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18b1 Note]]; read back your call sign, the runway and the hold short, not "Roger" or "Wilco" [[7:8|AC 91-73B 7f(4)]].

Its data block reads ASOS 135.375, then 1188 *L 58 122.7 with a circled C, then RP 26, 32. Obstacles, the Pittsfield RCO box on 122.05 and the town of Lenox are nearby.

f2.alt: Two not-to-scale drawings of a runway with a rectangular traffic pattern. In A, a dotted path crosses over midfield at 500 ft above pattern altitude, flies about 2 miles clear, descends to pattern altitude, turns back inbound and enters downwind at 45 degrees at midfield after yielding to downwind traffic. In B, a dotted path crosses at pattern altitude near midfield and turns onto downwind after yielding to traffic on the preferred 45 entry and on downwind.

f3.alt: Table of the six tower light gun signals: steady green, flashing green, steady red, flashing red, flashing white, and alternating red and green, with their meanings for vehicles and personnel, aircraft on the ground, and aircraft in flight.

In B the dashes end at the four-line holding position marking, with the note: prepare to stop unless cleared onto or across the runway by ATC.

scenario.title: Back in the left seat after five years
scenario.setup: You hold a private certificate and have not flown for five years. Today, after your flight review, you fly a rented Skyhawk from Hilltop, a non-towered Class G field, to Riverton, a Class D airport with a part-time tower that closes at 2000. Riverton's diagram shows a hot spot, HS 1, where Taxiway Charlie crosses Runway 18 near the end of Runway 24. You plan to come home after dark. (Hilltop and Riverton are made-up airports.)

questions.q: What should you review about Riverton before you leave home?
questions.a: NOTAMs and the ATIS for closed runways, taxiways and construction, and the airport diagram with its hot spots, to get the big picture of where an incursion could happen [[7:3|AC 91-73B 7b(1)]]. Plan the taxi just as you plan the flight [[15:16|AC 61-98E 2.3.6.2]].

questions.q: Departing Hilltop, when do you talk on the CTAF, and what do you check before taking the runway?
questions.a: Call before taxiing and before taxiing onto the runway [[33:207|AIM TBL 4-1-1]]. Before entering, make sure no aircraft is landing toward you or on your runway [[17:6|AC 90-66C 9.5.1]], and listen for no-radio traffic [[7:7|AC 91-73B 7d(12)]].

questions.q: Inbound to Riverton, when do you call the tower, and what must happen before you enter its Class D?
questions.a: Call about 15 miles out [[33:237|AIM 4-3-2a]]. Two-way radio communication must be established before you enter the Class D [[60:453|14 CFR 91.129(c)(1)]].

questions.q: After landing on 24, ground says: "Skyhawk three four X, taxi to the ramp via Charlie." Charlie crosses Runway 18 at HS 1. What do you do?
questions.a: Taxi on Charlie but stop at the Runway 18 holding position marking. A clearance to parking does not let you cross any runway [[33:264|AIM 4-3-21c Note 2]], and ATC issues an explicit clearance for every crossing [[33:260|AIM 4-3-18a5]]. Ask if unsure: "Skyhawk three four X, am I cleared to cross Runway 18?" [[16:10|AC 90-48E 10.3.4]].

questions.q: Approaching that hold line, you see yellow dashes on both sides of the taxiway centerline. What are they telling you?
questions.a: It is an enhanced taxiway centerline: a runway holding position marking is within 150 ft, so prepare to stop unless you are cleared onto or across the runway [[33:144|AIM 2-3-4b2]].

questions.q: You return at 2030, after the tower has closed. How does the arrival change, and who clears you across Runway 18?
questions.a: Riverton is now a non-towered airport: self-announce on the CTAF [[33:209|AIM 4-1-9g2]] and fly the 91.126 pattern flow, left unless marked otherwise [[17:4|AC 90-66C 8.2.1.1 Note]] [[60:451|14 CFR 91.126(b)]]. Nobody clears you: before crossing the hold line, make sure the runway is clear of aircraft, vehicles and people, including on final [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5a1]] [[1:342|PHAK 14-8]].

skills.do: Talk through and fly a non-towered arrival and departure (pattern direction, entry, departure path and every CTAF call), then taxi at a towered airport from ramp to runway and back, with correct readbacks, a stop at every hold line not cleared past, and correct reading of signs, markings and any light signals.
skills.practice: Pick a non-towered airport and a towered airport near you. From the chart and Chart Supplement, write the pattern direction, pattern altitude, CTAF and your calls for each leg [[17:5|AC 90-66C 9.1]] [[33:207|AIM TBL 4-1-1]]. Then, with the towered airport's diagram, highlight every hot spot and hold line on a likely taxi route and practice the readback out loud [[7:4|AC 91-73B 7b(2)]] [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18a9]]. Fly it with an instructor at your flight review, which covers airport markings and operations [[15:41|AC 61-98E E-2]] [[15:16|AC 61-98E 2.3.6.1]].

quiz.q: At a non-towered airport in Class G with no right-pattern markings, an airplane approaching to land must:
options: Enter on a 45 degree angle to midfield downwind
Make all turns to the left
Fly a straight-in if no one is in the pattern
Call the CTAF 10 miles out
quiz.why: 91.126(b) requires all turns to the left unless approved lights or markings show right turns [[60:451|14 CFR 91.126(b)]]. The FAA regulates pattern flow, not entry, so the 45 entry is a recommendation [[17:4|AC 90-66C 8.2.1]], and the 10-mile call comes from the AIM's table of recommended procedures [[33:207|AIM TBL 4-1-1]].

quiz.q: An airport has no tower, no FSS and no UNICOM. Where do you self-announce?
options: MULTICOM 122.9
The nearest tower's frequency
quiz.why: Use MULTICOM 122.9 for self-announce where there is no tower, FSS or UNICOM [[33:209|AIM 4-1-9g3]].

quiz.q: You choose a VFR straight-in at a non-towered airport. Which is true?
options: You have priority over aircraft in the pattern
Announce about 8 to 10 miles out and coordinate; you get no priority
No radio call is needed until short final
It is prohibited by 91.126
quiz.why: The FAA discourages straight-ins. If you fly one, self-announce 8 to about 10 miles out, coordinate, and know you get no priority [[17:8|AC 90-66C 9.11.1]].

quiz.q: At an airport with an operating control tower, which needs an ATC clearance under 91.129(i)?
options: Only takeoff and landing
Operating on a runway or taxiway, taking off and landing
Only crossing an active runway
Only taxiing at night
quiz.why: No one may operate on a runway or taxiway, take off or land at an airport with an operating tower without an appropriate clearance [[60:454|14 CFR 91.129(i)]].

quiz.q: Which items does the AIM say to always read back in taxi instructions?
options: The taxi route only
The runway assignment, any clearance to enter a runway, and any hold short or line up and wait instruction
Only the ATIS code
Nothing; "wilco" covers it
quiz.why: Always read back the runway assignment, any clearance to enter a specific runway, and any instruction to hold short of a runway or line up and wait [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18a9]].

quiz.q: You are in the pattern with a dead radio. The tower shows you a steady red light. What does it mean?
options: Airport unsafe, do not land
Give way to other aircraft and continue circling
Return for landing
Cleared to land
quiz.why: Steady red to an aircraft in flight means give way to other aircraft and continue circling [[60:451|14 CFR 91.125]]. Flashing red means airport unsafe [[60:451|14 CFR 91.125]].

quiz.q: Yellow dashes appear on both sides of the taxiway centerline. What is ahead?
options: A taxiway intersection within 50 ft
A runway holding position marking within about 150 ft
The end of the movement area
An ILS critical area
quiz.why: The enhanced taxiway centerline runs up to 150 ft before a runway holding position marking [[33:144|AIM 2-3-4b2]].

quiz.q: How is a hot spot shown on an FAA airport diagram?
options: A red box with "HS" inside
A brown open circle or ellipse leadered to a number such as HS 1
A yellow X
A dashed magenta line
quiz.why: Hot spots are a brown open circle or ellipse leadered to a hot spot number, described on the hot spot page in the front of the TPP [[2:124|Chart Users' Guide p 124]].

quiz.q: What does a Category D runway incursion mean?
options: A collision barely avoided
A loss of separation needing a time-critical response
Ample time and distance to avoid a collision
An incorrect presence on the runway's protected area with no immediate safety consequences
quiz.why: Category D meets the definition but has no immediate safety consequences [[15:15|AC 61-98E 2.3.2]]. A is a near collision, B needs a time-critical response, C has ample time and distance [[15:15|AC 61-98E 2.3.2]].

final_quiz.q: You arrive at 2200 at an airport whose part-time tower closed at 2100. The chart shows no RP. What do you do?
options: Call the closed tower anyway and wait for a light
Self-announce on the CTAF and fly a left pattern
Use any pattern direction; tower rules no longer apply
Fly a straight-in, since no one is controlling traffic
final_quiz.why: With the tower closed and no FSS, self-announce on the CTAF [[33:209|AIM 4-1-9g2]]. The 91.126 flow rules still apply when a towered airport operates as non-towered, and no RP means left traffic [[17:4|AC 90-66C 8.2.1.1 Note]].

final_quiz.q: Pittsfield's chart block reads "RP 26, 32." You will land on Runway 14. What pattern do you fly?
options: Right, because the airport has an RP note
Left, because only 26 and 32 have right traffic
Right, because 14 is the opposite of 32
Ask UNICOM; the chart does not say
final_quiz.why: RP lists only the runways with right traffic [[2:16|Chart Users' Guide p 16]]. All other runways use the standard left pattern [[33:240|AIM 4-3-3c]] [[60:451|14 CFR 91.126(b)]].

final_quiz.q: Ground: "Skyhawk three four X, Runway niner, taxi via Bravo, hold short of Runway four." Which readback is best?
options: "Roger, three four X."
"Wilco."
"Skyhawk three four X, Runway niner via Bravo, hold short Runway four."
"Three four X, Bravo to niner."
final_quiz.why: Read back the runway assignment and hold short with your call sign and the runway [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18a9]] [[7:8|AC 91-73B 7f(4)]]. "Roger" and "Wilco" are not enough, and ATC must get the hold short readback [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18b1 Note]].

final_quiz.q: Ground tells you to hold short of the Runway 27 ILS critical area. Where do you stop?
options: At the four-line runway holding position marking
With no part of the airplane past the ladder-shaped ILS holding position marking
At the runway edge
At the single dashed line
final_quiz.why: The ILS holding position marking is two solid lines joined by pairs of lines across the taxiway; stop so no part of the airplane extends beyond it [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5b]].

final_quiz.q: NORDO, you got a steady green on downwind. On short final the tower shows a flashing red light. What do you do?
options: Land; the steady green already cleared you
Go around and do not land: the airport is unsafe
Land and taxi clear of the runway
Circle and land on the other runway
final_quiz.why: A flashing red light to an aircraft in flight means airport unsafe, do not land [[60:451|14 CFR 91.125]]. The latest signal governs (application).

final_quiz.q: At night your radio has failed while you sit on a towered airport's ramp. How do you get the tower's attention?
options: Flash the strobes at the tower from the runway
Turn on the landing light and taxi, clear of the active runway, to where the tower can see it
Taxi onto the runway and wait
Blink the navigation lights from the hangar
final_quiz.why: Between sunset and sunrise, turn on a landing light and taxi clear of the active runway to a spot where the light is visible to the tower; leave it on until signals come [[33:257|AIM 4-3-13c]].

final_quiz.q: Cleared for takeoff, you begin rolling when red lights in two rows down the runway centerline turn on. What are they and what do you do?
options: Runway centerline lights: continue
Takeoff Hold Lights: stop if you safely can, and contact ATC
Stop bar: continue, since you were cleared
Runway guard lights: continue with caution
final_quiz.why: Takeoff Hold Lights show it is unsafe to take off. Stop if feasible and contact ATC to resolve the conflict [[33:128|AIM 2-1-6c3]].

final_quiz.q: After landing at a towered airport, your whole airplane has crossed the hold markings. Tower has said nothing more. What now?
options: Taxi to the ramp; you know the way
Hold there unless ATC has given further instructions
Switch to ground and taxi, then call
Back-taxi to the last exit
final_quiz.why: Once all parts of the airplane are past the holding position markings, hold unless ATC has issued further instructions [[33:264|AIM 4-3-21b]]. Change to ground when advised [[33:264|AIM 4-3-21c]].

final_quiz.q: You depart a non-towered satellite airport that lies inside a Class D. When must you talk to the Class D's ATC facility?
options: Before engine start
Before taking the runway
As soon as practicable after departing
Only if you will overfly the primary airport
final_quiz.why: From a satellite airport without an operating tower, establish and maintain two-way radio contact with the ATC facility for the Class D as soon as practicable after departing [[60:453|14 CFR 91.129(c)(2)(ii)]].

final_quiz.q: At night at an unfamiliar towered airport, you realize you might be on a runway, not a taxiway. Best action?
options: Stop right there and ask ground where you are
Do not stop on a runway; get off it, stop, tell ATC and ask for progressive taxi
Keep going; the next sign will tell you
Turn on the strobes and continue
final_quiz.why: Never stop on a runway when disoriented. Stop, advise ATC immediately and request progressive taxi if needed [[7:9|AC 91-73B 7g(5)]] [[7:6|AC 91-73B 7d(7)]]. Runways have white segmented centerlines; taxiways, continuous yellow [[7:9|AC 91-73B 7g(5)]].

final_quiz.q: Which CTAF call best follows the AIM and AC 90-66C?
options: "Traffic, blue and white Cessna, downwind for the active, any traffic please advise."
"Pittsfield traffic, Skyhawk one two three four X, entering right downwind runway two six, full stop, Pittsfield."
"Pittsfield traffic, Skyhawk three four X, downwind, number two for landing."
"Berkshire County traffic, Cessna downwind to two six."
final_quiz.why: Use the airport name at the start and end, the runway number and your call sign and type [[33:209|AIM 4-1-9g8]] [[17:7|AC 90-66C 9.8.1]]. "Please advise" is not recognized [[33:209|AIM 4-1-9g1]], don't announce your sequence [[17:13|AC 90-66C 10.1 Note]], and use the airport's name, not the area's, avoiding "to" [[17:12|AC 90-66C 10.1]] [[17:13|AC 90-66C 10.3]].

final_quiz.q: At a towered airport, ground told you to hold short of Runway 31. You stop with the nose past the runway holding position marking. No aircraft are near. How does the FAA's runway incursion definition treat it?
options: Not an incursion, because nothing came close
A runway incursion; with no immediate safety consequences it fits Category D
Only an incursion if ATC had to move another aircraft
Always Category A
final_quiz.why: Holding position markings mark the beginning of the runway safety area [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5a1 Note]], and mandatory signs mark where aircraft hold before entering a protected runway safety surface area [[19:24|AC 150/5340-18H 1-10]]. An incorrect presence on the protected area is an incursion [[15:14|AC 61-98E 2.3.1]], and Category D is one with no immediate safety consequences [[15:15|AC 61-98E 2.3.2]]. Calling your stop Category D is application of these definitions.

final_quiz.q: At night you approach a non-towered field with pilot-controlled lighting. The lights are already on. What should you do?
options: Nothing; they are on
Key the mike as directed anyway, so you are close enough and get a full 15 minutes
Key it once to keep them on
Call UNICOM to leave them on
final_quiz.why: Even when the lights are on, key the mike as directed when overflying or just before final, so the system hears you and gives a full 15 minutes [[33:132|AIM 2-1-8c]].

takeaways: Non-towered: 91.126 makes pattern turns left unless marked right; the FAA regulates flow, not entry.
Enter level at pattern altitude; announce 10 miles out and on each leg; airport name first and last.
Towered: talk before 4 NM up to 2,500 ft AGL (or before entering Class D), and get a clearance for every runway, taxiway, takeoff and landing.
Every runway crossing needs its own explicit "cross" clearance; read back runways and hold shorts with your call sign.
Solid yellow lines are on your side: stop there. Red signs mean a runway or protected area ahead.
Red RWSL or stop bar lights: never cross. Lights going out is not a clearance.
Review hot spots and NOTAMs before you taxi, and do heads-down work only when stopped.
cfi_notes: Refresher pilots trained before June 30, 2010 may still believe a runway assignment lets them cross intervening runways. PHAK 14-34 shows the change [[1:368|PHAK 14-34]], and AIM 4-3-18a5 is the current rule [[33:260|AIM 4-3-18a5]]. Ask them to taxi a route aloud.

The sources word readbacks differently. AC 61-98E says a taxi clearance readback "is mandatory" [[15:17|AC 61-98E 2.3.6.3.4]], and AC 91-73B says pilots "are required" to read back all clearances [[7:8|AC 91-73B 7f(4)]]. The AIM says pilots "should always read back" the runway assignment, any clearance to enter a runway, and any hold short or line up and wait instruction, and that ATC is required to obtain a readback of runway hold short instructions [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18a9, b1]]. 14 CFR 91.129 requires a clearance to operate on runways and taxiways but says nothing about readbacks [[60:454|14 CFR 91.129(i)]]. Teach the AIM items as what to always read back, and present the AC wording as FAA guidance rather than a regulation.

PHAK 14-31 still uses an older runway incursion definition (a collision hazard or loss of separation) [[1:365|PHAK 14-31]]. Teach the current FAA definition in AC 61-98E and AC 91-73B: any incorrect presence on the protected area [[15:14|AC 61-98E 2.3.1]].
AC 90-66C's Figure 1 caption says "RP 32", but the chart in it reads "RP 26, 32" [[17:5|AC 90-66C Figure 1]]. Good teaching moment: read the chart, not the caption.

AC 91-73B dates from 2012 and lists AC 90-66 under an older title [[7:1|AC 91-73B 4]]. The current edition in the sources is AC 90-66C (6/6/23), Non-Towered Airport Flight Operations [[17:1|AC 90-66C]].

Separate rule from advice. Regulation: 91.125, 91.126(b) and (d), 91.127, 91.129(c), (d), (f) and (i). Recommendation: 45 degree entries, 10-mile calls, pattern altitudes, upwind crossings [[17:4|AC 90-66C 8.2.1]].
For pilots who fly mostly at one airport, AC 61-98E notes some GA pilots ignore signage when familiar [[15:16|AC 61-98E 2.3.6.1]]. Have them name each sign on the way out to the runway.
Light signals are rare in practice. Drill the 91.125 table with the radio-failure case at the end of a flight review [[60:451|14 CFR 91.125]] [[60:453|14 CFR 91.129(d)(2)]].
gaps: The sources do not define "in the vicinity of an airport" in 91.126 and 91.127 with a distance. AC 90-66C uses a 10-mile radius only for CTAF practice.
Each airport's hot spot descriptions, pattern altitude, CTAF and lighting frequency are in the Chart Supplement and the Terminal Procedures hot spot page, which are not in the sources.
Controller procedures (FAA Order JO 7110.65) and the runway incursion order (FAA Order 7050.1) are cited by the sources but not included.
Part 93 special traffic rules and LAHSO details are only mentioned here; LAHSO acceptance belongs with landing performance from the POH/AFM.
The 2025 amendment listed under 91.126 (Amdt. 91-381) is shown without what it changed; the sources do not say.

activities.title: Pattern and runway numbers
activities.intro: Work it out, then type your answer.

items.q: Pittsfield's field elevation is 1,188 ft MSL and its pattern is 1,000 ft AGL. No jets are based there. You arrive from the upwind side and cross midfield at the AFH's normal altitude. What MSL altitude is that?
items.why: Cross at least 500 ft above pattern altitude, normally 1,500 ft AGL [[24:168|AFH 8-4]] [[17:23|AC 90-66C A-5]]. 1,188 + 1,000 + 500 = 2,688 ft MSL. Field elevation from the chart [[17:5|AC 90-66C Figure 1]].

items.q: Same airport. Staying in the pattern after takeoff, what is the lowest MSL altitude at which you should start the crosswind turn?
items.why: Turn crosswind past the departure end and within 300 ft of pattern altitude [[17:15|AC 90-66C 11.7]]. Pattern altitude 1,188 + 1,000 = 2,188; 2,188 - 300 = 1,888 ft MSL.

items.q: Takeoff Hold Lights start 375 ft from the departure threshold and run 1,500 ft. How far from the threshold do they end?
Application: you taxi at 10 knots when the enhanced centerline dashes begin 150 ft before the hold line. About how many seconds until you reach the line?
items.why: The dashes extend up to 150 ft before the runway holding position marking [[33:144|AIM 2-3-4b2]]. 10 knots = 10 x 6,076 / 3,600 = 16.9 ft per second; 150 / 16.9 = 8.9 seconds.

activities.title: True or false: runway incursions
activities.intro: Decide if each statement is true or false.

cards.s: It only counts as a runway incursion if two aircraft nearly collide.
cards.why: False. Any incorrect presence on the protected area counts [[15:14|AC 61-98E 2.3.1]]; Category D has no immediate safety consequences [[15:15|AC 61-98E 2.3.2]].

cards.s: In FY 2012, pilot deviations caused most runway incursions, and GA pilots caused more than 80 percent of those deviations.
cards.why: True: 63 percent were pilot deviations, and GA pilots were responsible for more than 80 percent of them [[15:15|AC 61-98E 2.3.3]].

cards.s: Pilots who know an airport well can be more likely to ignore its signs.
cards.why: True. AC 61-98E notes some GA pilots ignore signage at airports they know [[15:16|AC 61-98E 2.3.6.1]].

cards.s: Once you are cleared to cross a runway, there is no need to look before crossing.
cards.why: False. Scan the full length of the runway and the final approach before entering or crossing, even with a clearance [[1:368|PHAK 14-34]] [[7:6|AC 91-73B 7d(4)]].

cards.s: A hot spot is a place where jet blast is a known problem.
cards.why: False. It is a place with a history of potential risk of collision or runway incursion [[34:358|PCG H-3]].

cards.s: You expected the usual "cross Runway 31" but heard "hold short of Runway 31." You hold short.
cards.why: True. Follow the clearance actually received, not the one you expected [[7:4|AC 91-73B 7b(2) Caution]].

cards.s: Writing taxi instructions down is only for student pilots.
cards.why: False. Writing down instructions reduces misunderstanding and forgetting, especially for complex clearances or unfamiliar airports [[7:7|AC 91-73B 7e]] [[1:367|PHAK 14-33]].

activities.title: Hilltop to Riverton and back
activities.intro: You fly N1234X, a Skyhawk, from Hilltop, a non-towered Class G field, to Riverton, a Class D airport. Riverton's hot spot HS 1 is where Taxiway Charlie crosses Runway 18. (Made-up airports.)

steps.s: At Hilltop you are holding short of Runway 30, ready to go. An RV calls a 3-mile final for Runway 12, the opposite end. What do you do?
options: Take Runway 30 now and go quickly
Hold short, let the RV land, then announce and go
Ask "any traffic in the area, please advise"
Back-taxi on 30 while the RV is still out
steps.why: Don't enter the runway until you have verified there is no landing traffic opposite or aligned with your runway [[17:6|AC 90-66C 9.5.1]]. "Please advise" is not a recognized call [[33:209|AIM 4-1-9g1]], and back-taxiing is discouraged at non-towered airports [[17:13|AC 90-66C 10.4.2 Note]].

steps.s: You are 15 miles from Riverton. When do you call the tower?
options: Now, so radio contact is set before you enter the Class D
At 4 NM
On downwind
After landing, to ground
steps.why: Initial call about 15 miles out [[33:237|AIM 4-3-2a]]; two-way radio communication must be established before entering Class D [[60:453|14 CFR 91.129(c)(1)]].

steps.s: After landing, ground says: "Three four X, taxi to the ramp via Charlie." Charlie crosses Runway 18 at HS 1. What do you do at Runway 18?
options: Cross; the clearance to the ramp covers it
Stop at the hold line and get an explicit crossing clearance
Cross quickly if no one is on final
Turn around and use another taxiway
steps.why: A taxi clearance to parking does not authorize crossing any runway [[33:264|AIM 4-3-21c Note 2]]; ATC issues an explicit clearance for every crossing [[33:260|AIM 4-3-18a5]].

steps.s: Ground says "cross Runway 18." At the hold line, the red in-pavement Runway Entrance Lights are lit. What now?
options: Cross: you have a clearance
Stay stopped, tell ground you are holding for red runway lights, and reconfirm
Cross quickly before the traffic arrives
Wait for the lights to go out, then cross without calling
steps.why: When you see red RELs, stop at the hold line or stay stopped and contact ATC if the clearance conflicts with the lights [[33:127|AIM 2-1-6b4]]. Never cross red lights, and lights going out is not a clearance [[33:129|AIM 2-1-6d3-4]].

steps.s: Leaving at dusk, tower says "Runway two four, line up and wait," with no reason given. Ninety seconds pass in silence. What do you do?
options: Start the takeoff; no one is landing
Call the tower and ask
Exit the runway without telling anyone
Turn off all lights and wait
steps.why: With no reason given, expect a call within 90 seconds; if none comes, call ATC [[7:6|AC 91-73B 7d(9)]] [[1:369|PHAK 14-35]]. LUAW is not a takeoff clearance [[1:368|PHAK 14-34]].
